Penile Transplant

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The first successful penile transplant in the world gives hope to 100s of SA men who have lost their penis during traditional circumcisions rites

Summary:
South Africa has achieved another medical first, a team of doctors from Stellenbosch University did the first successful penile transplant in the world. The patient had the operation in December 2014 and 5 weeks later had full sexual function. The man lost his penis at the age of 19 due to a botched traditional circumcision and was left with a 1 cm stump. Urologist Prof Andre Van der Merwe led a team of plastic surgeons and immunologist and during a 9 hour operation successful attached a transplanted a penis from an organ donor

Further information:
Twice a year in June and December 100’s of young Xhosa boys go to the “bush” to undergo a traditional rite of passage; they are circumcised by traditional doctors and kept far from any Western Medicine learning the ways of their culture and how to be responsible men. If they survive they are welcomed back into the community as men. Young Xhosa boys are put under enormous social pressure from the men in their community and will only be treated as an adult if they undergo the ritual and survive. Anybody who gets ill and does not complete the process is never recognised as a man. Woman are not allowed any contact with their sons during this 3 weeks to 2 months period, they have no cellphones and are completely isolated from the outside world kept almost like prisoners .
There have been numerous attempts to make the practice more hygienic, measures by the Health Department to set up centres where the boys can be housed and traditional practices supervised but have largely been unsuccessful. As a result 919 boys have died since 1995 and twice that number has lost their penis. After the circumcision is done the boys’ penis are tightly bound and they are given no water and eat dry food for the first week in an attempt to stop them urinating. Frequently far more than the foreskin is removed creating a large wound, sometimes the tip of the penis is cut off and they bleed out, other times infection sets in, and if the penis is too tightly bound it can become gangrenous and fall off. These boys are expected to suffer in silence, complaining is seen as weakness and seeking medical help a failure.
To date there have been attempts to do penile reconstructions from flesh taken from the abdomen but these have been purely to restore urinary function. These”penises” have never been sexually functional. The loss of a penis is so devastating for young men that many have committed suicide. They will never be men in the eyes of the community.
In this context Stellenbosch University started a study in 2010. The study was conducted as part of the Kidney Transplant Unit at Tygerberg Hospital as it was deemed to have the most appropriate infra- structure. One of the biggest hurdles has been getting families to donate the penis of their dead relatives. Organ donation is a problem generally but somehow donating a penis is a step to far for most people. Secondly the transplant must happen within 10 to 16 hours and the operation takes 9 hours.
Secondly the patient also has to understand and agree that they will be on immune suppressants for the rest of their lives. They have to visit the hospital once a month for monitoring because they face the very real danger of Cancer, Diabetes, High Blood pressure because they are on steroids for the rest of their lives. But despite knowing all these risks many men would rather have their penis. There are 9 more candidates in line for the operation as soon as a donor becomes available
Prof Van Der Merwe has been screening patents for the last 12 years and many patients do not qualify because of their lifestyles. There was great debate about whether it is ok to put a patient on immune suppressants when the loss of a penis is not a life threatening illness. The cost of the medication for the rest of their lives will be about R16000 a month to the State. The theatre cost are not any higher than a Kidney transplant but in the context of Tygerberg Hospital already having had its budget cut to inflation serious ethical questions have been raised.
Prof Van Der Merwe consulted Traditional Healers as part of his research and they did not have any adverse reaction to the transplant. Despite this great achievement for medical science and giving the victims who have lost their “manhood” a ray of hope, Penile transplants will probably remain beyond the reach of most victims of circumcision.

Press Release:


South African doctors make global medical history as they perform the world’s first successful penile transplant. Carte Blanche hears from the passionate team behind the procedure as we explore new hope for young men who have lost their penises through botched cultural circumcision.

Script:


Prof Van der Merwe “The things that made me persist with the project was the patients.They stick in your mind you go and sleep at night but the voice doesn’t go away constantly reminding me about them, constantly saying doc please you have to help us the stress is unbearable I cannot bear it
Script: Urologist Prof Andre van der Merwe head of the team who performed the world’s first successful penile transplant has found the worlds reaction rather surprising and has been inundated with requests for help
Prof Andre Van Der Merwe Of course there is multiple jokes. But men who has been willing or they have been having new courage to speak about their problem emailed me directly. One male from the US which is s scientist he is now 32 he was born without a penis, he said he is so encouraged by this. This really is a project about hope in the end
Script: Prof van der Merwe was driven to address a peculiarly South Africa problem. Twice a year 1000’s of young Xhosa men leave their families to go into the mountains to undergo traditional circumcision, tragically many never return, and their deaths are shrouded in secrecy. Roughly 919 people have died and twice that amount has lost their penises since 1995. Prof Van der Merwe was so disturbed by what he was witnessing in the wards of Tygerberg Hospital that 7 years ago he began his research
Prof Andre Van Der Merwe After the circumcision event the buckskin is wrapped in a fashion that it covers the whole penis, then if it is wrapped too tight and not removed quickly enough then there will be no blood flow into the penis then this whole penis becomes gangrenous in other words it dies and then often infection sets in and these young men are restricted on the amount of fluid that they can drink so their kidneys are already stressed and then if it becomes septicaemia. On a stressed kidney they often go into acute renal failure and die from septicaemia
Script: One of his first recruits to assist him in his study was organ transplant co-ordinator at Tygerberg hospital Sister Bailey. She is a highly skilled counsellor and does all the psychological preparation of the kidney transplant patients
Sister Bertha Bailey “In our culture because you are a woman you are not supposed to know what is going on there it’s more like a secret that happens only in men’s territory, of course I know I need to keep that secret and I don’t talk about it in fact but I am glad I know what is going on there, what’s happening as a mother”
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “One of my patients on the waiting list the friend with him in the hut died and the body wasn’t removed very quickly he himself suffered septicaemia was ventilated in hospital, 18 or 19 years old they are not supposed to go to Western Medical care they do not have the social skills to deal with the situation they do not have the support they are some of the guys on my list have not even told their parents, and they still live with their parents. They are carrying a huge burden
Sister Bertha Bailey “When they leave my office I cry, I am telling myself this could have been my own son
Script: Sister Bailey has been working with the group of 10 young men since 2010 encouraging them to hold on, but it’s been extremely difficult to find a donor
Link “The reluctance of most South Africans to donate their organs is complicated by what professor van der Merwe describes as the yuk factor even those who are prepared to donate other organs are put off by the idea of donating a penis
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe 01 12 10 I have given probably up about 4 times on this project. We thought we are going to get support from all over the country all the transplant centres and everybody in transplantation, it was a big mistake it created a some form of reaction in some of our colleagues that surprised us, people are going to think we are going to use the penis for muti
Script: There is a massive shortage of organ donors and 100s of people waiting for life saving transplants, asking for a penis could compromise the requests for vital organs
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “ Then it dawned on me that the family do not want to send a donor to the grave without a penis, ….we immediately changed our protocol to that we are going say we either going to take just the penis without the skin or we are going to make a penis from skin. Then it happened at the most unexpected of times.
Script: Finally a family donated their brain dead relative’s entire body. The heart, two lungs, liver, kidney and penis were all available. Prof van der Merwe was so shocked he made the team check with the relatives 3 times before he set everything into motion.
Prof Andre Van Der Merwe “I had to make a call here, I thought the kidney would not be able to wait as long as the penis being more sensitive tissue
Script: The team of doctors arrived having already worked long days on other procedures. The same team harvested the organs, waited for theatre to be cleaned and then performed a difficult 4 hour kidney transplant on another patient before they could begin the pioneering penile transplant e 21 year old
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe Some people think you just connect a few tubes …but after ritual circumcision the anatomy of the a proximal penis is pretty much destroyed
Script. It was Micro and reconstructive plastic surgeon Prof Frank Greawe job to find all the blood vessels and the nerves and reconnect them
Frank Greawe “When we got there at 3 o’clock we stated opening up looking at the blood vessels and the next surprise was everything was basically obliterated, destroyed the blood vessels fibrotic
John Because of the amputation
Frank Greawe Because of the infection that led to the whole problem everything was stuck together the tissue we had to carefully carefully dissect it until we realised the blood vessels there we cant use them. So we had to make a different plan and we and we went into the lower abdominal area and we did a little incision in the lower abdomen and we identified a blood vessel we work a lot with, we dissected it out that it was long enough and then we basically looped it down into the peripheral area under the skin and tunnelled it through and brought it out where the blood vessels were sutured
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “It was a long 9 hours still when it reaches between 4 o’clock and 5 o’clock operating, those hours are very long hours to operate but we pushed through
Script: The same theatre had to be used for all three procedures; it took 21 hours and with just two breaks in between to clean the theatre
Frank Greawe “The beautiful thing about that happened was our team work , I could never have done this without Andre doing all the ground work, I could not have done it without Rafique , we could have not done it without each other
Script: Nephrologist Professor Rafique Moosa specialises in immune suppression. He says the body’s natural reaction is to reject anything it identifies as not its own and so all transplants require a cocktail of drugs to suppress this reaction
Prof Moosa “The risk of acute rejection is in the initial part after the transplant so the first few weeks, the first months the risk is the greatest, so in time hopefully after 3-6 months we should be able to reduce the amount of immunosuppression that the patient actually receives. The greatest risk is in terms of infections especially in our community we are concerned about TB, viral infections are always a risk so what we do is we pre-empt that. Then there are other complications we look out for there is a risk of diabetes for example, the risk of bone disease. So with our experience with patients with kidney transplants we are aware of these complications
Script: The Penile transplant recipients have to be carefully assessed and psychologically prepared. There is massive swelling after the operation, they remain in isolation for a month and the tough bit is they have to accept that they will be on medication for the rest of their lives no matter how well they feel.
JOHN “Also is it important for the donor to be the same race?”
Prof Van der Merwe “Most of our donors are not ethnic black, and obviously all our recipients are ethnic black so I had to put it to the patients are they willing to receive a white penis on the basis that once the graft has taken I will remove the white skin I will then Transplant skin from the inside of his leg onto the shaft of the penis and then we will tattoo the glance or the head of the penis in a fitting colour”
LINK: “We were hoping to speak to one of the young men on the waiting list but after initially agreeing to the interview he pulled out fearing possible ostracism from his local community and apparently that is a common response from people in the same predicament.
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “ I think it is completely justified to do it on these patients They are seeing themselves and seen by the community as dead and they often commit suicide. We would never do a penile transplant for vanity the immune suppression is just too toxic
Sister Bertha Bailey “One of them I spoke to he has been relocating a lot because he told me that if he finds out that people know about it and then he will move
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “I interviewed Xhosa speaking people that are in leadership and I had a uniform response that it would be a wonderful thing. They also alerted me to the fact that these men even have a pecking order on how much of a stump is left. One male told me that if we can give a man a penis back after he lost it in a traditional circumcision the words he used were I will bring him back to life from the dead
Script: The 21 year who received the transplant in December 2014, has certainly has been brought back to life, much to Prof’s surprise he had his first sexual experience a mere 5 weeks after the op
Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “I have spoken to him and a few occasions and the response is yes I am fine and why wouldn’t I be so I am not sure how conscious he is about his place in history all I know , what I really know about him is that he has closed the door on his history now and he is looking forward he has accepted that organ as his own and the most incredible thing is his girlfriend too “
John: “Is he a very different young man after this operation?”
Sister Bertha Bailey “He had that smile that wasn’t going away even when you see him, he dresses up like a star. The one thing he is never tell me whether he has used it because I guess he was respecting me as a mother so when I asked him have you done anything no I didn’t “

So we had to make a different plan and we and we went into the lower abdominal area and we did a little incision in the lower abdomen and we identified a blood vessel we work a lot with, we dissected it out that it was long enough and then we basically looped it down into the peripheral area under the skin and tunnelled it through and brought it out where the blood vessels were sutured Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “It was a long 9 hours still when it reaches between 4 o’clock and 5 o’clock operating, those hours are very long hours to operate but we pushed through Script: The same theatre had to be used for all three procedures; it took 21 hours and with just two breaks in between to clean the theatre Frank Greawe “The beautiful thing about that happened was our team work , I could never have done this without Andre doing all the ground work, I could not have done it without Rafique , we could have not done it without each other Script: Nephrologist Professor Rafique Moosa specialises in immune suppression. He says the body’s natural reaction is to reject anything it identifies as not its own and so all transplants require a cocktail of drugs to suppress this reaction Prof Moosa “The risk of acute rejection is in the initial part after the transplant so the first few weeks, the first months the risk is the greatest, so in time hopefully after 3-6 months we should be able to reduce the amount of immunosuppression that the patient actually receives. The greatest risk is in terms of infections especially in our community we are concerned about TB, viral infections are always a risk so what we do is we pre-empt that. Then there are other complications we look out for there is a risk of diabetes for example, the risk of bone disease. So with our experience with patients with kidney transplants we are aware of these complications Script: The Penile transplant recipients have to be carefully assessed and psychologically prepared. There is massive swelling after the operation, they remain in isolation for a month and the tough bit is they have to accept that they will be on medication for the rest of their lives no matter how well they feel. JOHN “Also is it important for the donor to be the same race?” Prof Van der Merwe “Most of our donors are not ethnic black, and obviously all our recipients are ethnic black so I had to put it to the patients are they willing to receive a white penis on the basis that once the graft has taken I will remove the white skin I will then Transplant skin from the inside of his leg onto the shaft of the penis and then we will tattoo the glance or the head of the penis in a fitting colour” LINK: “We were hoping to speak to one of the young men on the waiting list but after initially agreeing to the interview he pulled out fearing possible ostracism from his local community and apparently that is a common response from people in the same predicament. Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “ I think it is completely justified to do it on these patients They are seeing themselves and seen by the community as dead and they often commit suicide. We would never do a penile transplant for vanity the immune suppression is just too toxic Sister Bertha Bailey “One of them I spoke to he has been relocating a lot because he told me that if he finds out that people know about it and then he will move Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “I interviewed Xhosa speaking people that are in leadership and I had a uniform response that it would be a wonderful thing. They also alerted me to the fact that these men even have a pecking order on how much of a stump is left. One male told me that if we can give a man a penis back after he lost it in a traditional circumcision the words he used were I will bring him back to life from the dead Script: The 21 year who received the transplant in December 2014, has certainly has been brought back to life, much to Prof’s surprise he had his first sexual experience a mere 5 weeks after the op Pro Andre Van Der Merwe “I have spoken to him and a few occasions and the response is yes I am fine and why wouldn’t I be so I am not sure how conscious he is about his place in history all I know , what I really know about him is that he has closed the door on his history now and he is looking forward he has accepted that organ as his own and the most incredible thing is his girlfriend too “ John: “Is he a very different young man after this operation?” Sister Bertha Bailey “He had that smile that wasn’t going away even when you see him, he dresses up like a star. The one thing he is never tell me whether he has used it because I guess he was respecting me as a mother so when I asked him have you done anything no I didn’t “ Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Penile Transplant (4526 ) lizfish@iafrica.com 27 March 2015

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The first successful penile transplant in the world gives hope to 100s of SA men who have lost their penis during traditional circumcisions rites
metadata.Summary: South Africa has achieved another medical first, a team of doctors from Stellenbosch University did the first successful penile transplant in the world. The patient had the operation in December 2014 and 5 weeks later had full sexual function. The man lost his penis at the age of 19 due to a botched traditional circumcision and was left with a 1 cm stump. Urologist Prof Andre Van der Merwe led a team of plastic surgeons and immunologist and during a 9 hour operation successful attached a transplanted a penis from an organ donor
metadata.Further information: Twice a year in June and December 100’s of young Xhosa boys go to the “bush” to undergo a traditional rite of passage; they are circumcised by traditional doctors and kept far from any Western Medicine learning the ways of their culture and how to be responsible men. If they survive they are welcomed back into the community as men. Young Xhosa boys are put under enormous social pressure from the men in their community and will only be treated as an adult if they undergo the ritual and survive. Anybody who gets ill and does not complete the process is never recognised as a man. Woman are not allowed any contact with their sons during this 3 weeks to 2 months period, they have no cellphones and are completely isolated from the outside world kept almost like prisoners . There have been numerous attempts to make the practice more hygienic, measures by the Health Department to set up centres where the boys can be housed and traditional practices supervised but have largely been unsuccessful. As a result 919 boys have died since 1995 and twice that number has lost their penis. After the circumcision is done the boys’ penis are tightly bound and they are given no water and eat dry food for the first week in an attempt to stop them urinating. Frequently far more than the foreskin is removed creating a large wound, sometimes the tip of the penis is cut off and they bleed out, other times infection sets in, and if the penis is too tightly bound it can become gangrenous and fall off. These boys are expected to suffer in silence, complaining is seen as weakness and seeking medical help a failure. To date there have been attempts to do penile reconstructions from flesh taken from the abdomen but these have been purely to restore urinary function. These”penises” have never been sexually functional. The loss of a penis is so devastating for young men that many have committed suicide. They will never be men in the eyes of the community. In this context Stellenbosch University started a study in 2010. The study was conducted as part of the Kidney Transplant Unit at Tygerberg Hospital as it was deemed to have the most appropriate infra- structure. One of the biggest hurdles has been getting families to donate the penis of their dead relatives. Organ donation is a problem generally but somehow donating a penis is a step to far for most people. Secondly the transplant must happen within 10 to 16 hours and the operation takes 9 hours. Secondly the patient also has to understand and agree that they will be on immune suppressants for the rest of their lives. They have to visit the hospital once a month for monitoring because they face the very real danger of Cancer, Diabetes, High Blood pressure because they are on steroids for the rest of their lives. But despite knowing all these risks many men would rather have their penis. There are 9 more candidates in line for the operation as soon as a donor becomes available Prof Van Der Merwe has been screening patents for the last 12 years and many patients do not qualify because of their lifestyles. There was great debate about whether it is ok to put a patient on immune suppressants when the loss of a penis is not a life threatening illness. The cost of the medication for the rest of their lives will be about R16000 a month to the State. The theatre cost are not any higher than a Kidney transplant but in the context of Tygerberg Hospital already having had its budget cut to inflation serious ethical questions have been raised. Prof Van Der Merwe consulted Traditional Healers as part of his research and they did not have any adverse reaction to the transplant. Despite this great achievement for medical science and giving the victims who have lost their “manhood” a ray of hope, Penile transplants will probably remain beyond the reach of most victims of circumcision.
